When calculating car fuel consumption, it is useful to understand both litres per 100 kilometres and miles per gallon. A vehicle that consumes 8 L/100 km (25.9 US mpg) uses 8 litres of fuel (2.11 US gallons) to travel 100 km (62.14 miles). If a car has a 50 L (13.21 US gallon) fuel tank, it can travel approximately 625 km (388.36 miles) under those consumption conditions. Actual fuel economy can vary depending on traffic, speed, and driving habits.

When heating a home, energy consumption may be measured in kilowatt-hours and British thermal units. Using 10 kWh (36,509.9 BTU) of energy provides the same energy quantity in either unit. A 2 kW (6,824 BTU/h) electric heater operating for 5 hours (300 minutes) consumes 10 kWh (34,121.4 BTU) of electricity. If electricity costs $0.15 per kWh (approximately $0.044 per 1,000 BTU), the total operating cost is $1.50 (150 cents).
